sections.h2: How fast can I sell a house in North Miami Beach?
sections.html:
A sale in North Miami Beach can close as quickly as the buyer and title company can finish their work, and the choices that decide the speed are who buys, how the buyer pays and what the title search turns up. A cash buyer skips mortgage underwriting, which removes the longest waiting period. A traditional listing gives you a wider pool of buyers but adds showings, an inspection period and a lender's timeline.

The city is small and dense, and its housing stock reflects that. The Census Bureau counts 46,236 residents in July 2025 living on about 4.84 square miles, and only 52.2 percent of homes are owner occupied. That mix of owners and renters matters when you sell, because buyers here range from families to investors who plan to rent the property out.

  • Cash offer: no appraisal contingency from a lender, a closing date you can often choose, and usually a sale as is.
  • Agent listing: more exposure and often a higher price, with repairs, showings and a longer calendar.
  • For sale by owner: no listing commission, but you handle disclosures, contracts and buyer screening yourself.

sections.h2: What is North Miami Beach like for a home seller?
sections.html:
North Miami Beach is an older, fully built suburb in northeast Miami-Dade County, laid out on a deliberate street plan with wide avenues. The city's own history page explains that its founder planned a "perfect city" in 1917 with 80 foot residential streets and 100 to 125 foot business thoroughfares, and that today's grid still follows that plan. Two of the original avenues are now Northeast 172nd Street and Northeast 19th Avenue.

The place began as the farming community of Ojus and the townsite of Fulford. Rock mining in the early 1900s left behind lakes, including Maule Lake and the lakes in the Sky Lake neighborhood, so some homes sit beside water that was once a quarry. The city incorporated as Fulford in 1927 after the 1926 hurricane, and a new charter in 1931 changed the name to North Miami Beach. A 1958 charter set up the council and manager form of government that the city still uses.

Landmarks buyers recognize include Greynolds Park, which opened as a county park in 1936 on an abandoned quarry site, and the Ancient Spanish Monastery on West Dixie Highway. State Road 826, also called North Miami Beach Boulevard, opened in 1951, and the 163rd Street shopping center followed in 1956. Residents commute along these corridors, and the Census Bureau puts the mean travel time to work at 30.1 minutes.

sections.h2: What does a cash sale cost in North Miami Beach?
sections.html:
The main state cost is documentary stamp tax on the deed, and North Miami Beach follows Miami-Dade County's rate rather than the 70 cent rate used in most counties. The Florida Department of Revenue says Miami-Dade charges 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, and that the surtax is not due on a document that transfers only a single-family dwelling. See the department's documentary stamp tax page for the exact wording.

All parties to the deed are liable to the state, even when the contract says one side pays. Your contract decides who actually covers it, so settle that in writing before you accept an offer. The clerk also charges recording fees: Florida law sets $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page of a deed, with a few small additional charges.

  • Deed stamp tax: use the Miami-Dade rate described above and ask the title company to calculate it.
  • Recording fees: set by statute section 28.24 and collected at recording.
  • Payoff of any mortgage, lien or past due tax: taken from your proceeds at closing.
  • Prorated property tax: the current year's bill is divided between seller and buyer by closing date.

sections.h2: How does Miami-Dade County property tax affect my sale?
sections.html:
The Miami-Dade Property Appraiser values your home as of January 1, and the tax bill arrives in November. Florida's calendar for all counties has the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes mailed in August, with a petition window of 25 days after it, and an early payment discount that steps down from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February.

Your homestead exemption ends with the sale, and the buyer must apply for his or her own. The county appraiser's homestead page says applications are due by March 1 and that property owners can be back taxed for ten years, with a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent annual interest, if they fail to report a change that ends eligibility. Renting the home is one such change.

The same page describes Amendment 3, which Florida voters approved on November 3, 2026. It raises the non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 for tax year 2027 and $250,000 for 2028 for owners who established Florida residency by December 31, 2026, and the school board portion stays at $25,000. A buyer who is new to Florida may qualify for a smaller amount at first. Ask a buyer's agent how this affects the price they will pay.

Under Save Our Homes, the state's cap limits the yearly rise in a homestead's assessed value, but a sale resets the property to just value the following January 1. That is why a buyer's first full bill can be well above yours. The Florida Department of Revenue explains the cap and the reset on its Save Our Homes guide.

sections.h2: Can I sell if the house needs repairs or has code problems?
sections.html:
Yes, a house can be sold with open repairs, but permits and code violations travel with the property, so find out what is open before you list. North Miami Beach runs its permits, inspections and code violations through the eDMS online portal, where you can search records, see violations and request inspections without calling the office.

Unpermitted work is the most common surprise. A porch enclosure, a converted garage or a bathroom added without a permit can stall a lender-backed sale, because the appraiser and the insurer will ask about it. Cash buyers often accept that risk, but they will lower the offer to cover it.

  • Search the address in the city's permit portal for open permits and violations.
  • Gather receipts for roof, windows, electrical and plumbing work.
  • Ask the title company for a lien search before you sign a contract.
  • If you rent the house, note the tenant's lease dates, because a buyer will want to know them.

sections.h2: What if I own a rental or inherited house in North Miami Beach?
sections.html:
A rented house can be sold with the tenant in place, and an inherited house can be sold once the estate has authority to convey it. In both cases the buyer will ask for proof of who may sign the deed, so gather the lease, the death certificate or the court papers early.

Short-term rentals add a local layer. North Miami Beach has a registration application for owners who list on platforms such as Airbnb or VRBO. Confirm the current rules with the city's Community Development office before you advertise a property as a short-term rental, because a buyer who plans to continue the use will ask whether the registration transfers.

Florida's conveyance statute requires a deed for land to be in writing and signed in front of two witnesses, and witnessing can be done by audio-video technology. Quitclaim deeds and contracts for deed are taxable documents for stamp tax purposes, according to the Department of Revenue, so a transfer among relatives is not automatically free of tax.

sections.h2: What steps lead from offer to closing in North Miami Beach?
sections.html:
The path has six steps, and most of the waiting happens inside the title company's work. Dates in the contract control everything, so write them down.

  • Collect the deed, mortgage payoff statement, association contact and last tax bill.
  • Compare a cash offer, a listing price and your net after costs.
  • Sign a contract that names who pays stamp tax and which repairs, if any, you will do.
  • The title company searches for liens, open permits and unpaid taxes.
  • You sign the deed before witnesses or a notary and deliver keys on the agreed day.
  • The clerk records the deed and collects the stamp tax.

Homeowners association or condominium buildings add an estoppel letter and sometimes board approval, so start those requests early. Cash buyers can often shorten the list, but the title search cannot be skipped.

faqs.q: Who pays documentary stamp tax on a North Miami Beach home sale?
faqs.a: The contract decides who pays, but the state holds every party to the deed liable. For Miami-Dade, the Department of Revenue prints 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, and the surtax is not due on a document that transfers only a single-family dwelling. Have the title company calculate the tax for your deed.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The buyer must file a new application with the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser by March 1. Your exemption ends with the sale, and the property is reassessed at just value the next January 1.

faqs.q: What is Amendment 3 and does it change my sale?
faqs.a: Amendment 3 is a constitutional change that the county appraiser says Florida voters approved on November 3, 2026. It raises the non-school homestead exemption for 2027 and 2028 for qualifying owners. It may affect how buyers think about carrying costs, but it does not change the deed process.

faqs.q: Can I sell a North Miami Beach house with open permits?
faqs.a: Yes, but the buyer will see the open permits in a title or permit search. Expect a lower cash offer or a request that you close the permit first. Search the address in the city's eDMS portal before you list.

faqs.q: How do I compare a cash offer with a listing?
faqs.a: Compare your estimated net, not the headline price. Subtract commission, repairs, carrying costs and the time you would wait for a lender-backed buyer, then compare that with the cash figure after the buyer's stated costs.
